articles.title: M11 Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP); International Council for Harmonisation; Guidance for Industry; Availability
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of a final guidance for industry entitled "M11 Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP)." The guidance was prepared under the auspices of the International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH). The guidance includes three documents: a guidance, a template, and a technical specification document. The guidance provides the rationale and recommendations for implementing a harmonized digital clinical trial protocol. The template features standardized content structure and formatting, including headers and common text elements. The technical specification document contains harmonized terminologies and standardized data fields to enable electronic exchange of clinical protocol information. The intent of the guidance is to create an internationally harmonized standard for the content and exchange of clinical trial protocol information, facilitating the review and assessment by regulators, sponsors, ethical oversight bodies, investigators, and other stakeholders. This guidance finalizes the draft guidances "M11 Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP)" issued on December 22, 2022 (87 FR 78696), and "M11 Technical Specification: Clinical Electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol" issued on June 6, 2025 (90 FR 24146).

The guidance provides information for manufacturers and contract laboratories that perform PER studies to assist in designing, conducting, evaluating, and reporting PER studies. The guidance explains "appropriate modifications" of AOAC Official Method 960.48 (the AOAC Method) with the aim of supporting industry in successfully conducting PER studies that demonstrate that a new infant formula meets the quality factor of sufficient biological quality of protein when fed as the sole source of nutrition. articles.title: Notice of Decision Not To Designate Hepatitis Delta Virus Diseases as an Addition to the Current List of Tropical Diseases in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act
articles.summary: In response to a suggestion by Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Gilead) that was submitted to the public docket FDA-2008-N-0567 on February 14, 2022, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) has analyzed whether hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection meets the statutory criteria for designation as a "tropical disease" under Section 524 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act). Specifically, the Agency has analyzed whether there is "no significant market in developed nations" for drugs for HDV infections and whether HDV "disproportionately affects poor and marginalized populations," both of which are statutory criteria for designation as a "tropical disease." At this time, the Agency cannot conclude that HDV infection meets the statutory criteria for addition to the list of tropical diseases under the FD&C Act; therefore, FDA declines to add it to the list of tropical diseases.

articles.summary: On May 28, 2010, the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) issued Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) guidance related to the "generic" clearance process. Generally, this is an expedited process by which agencies may obtain OMB's approval of collection of information requests that are "usually voluntary, low-burden, and uncontroversial collections," do not raise any substantive or policy issues, and do not require policy or methodological review. The process requires the submission of an overarching plan that defines the scope of the individual collections that would fall under its umbrella. On October 23, 2011, OMB approved our initial request to use the generic clearance process under control number 0938-1148 (CMS-10398). It was last approved on April 26, 2021, via the standard PRA process which included the publication of 60- and 30-day Federal Register notices. The scope of the April 2021 umbrella accounts for Medicaid and CHIP State plan amendments, waivers, demonstrations, and reporting. This Federal Register notice seeks public comment on one or more of our collection of information requests that we believe are generic and fall within the scope of the umbrella. Interested persons are invited to submit comments regarding our burden estimates or any other aspect of this collection of information, including: the necessity and utility of the proposed information collection for the proper performance of the agency's functions, the accuracy of the estimated burden, ways to enhance the quality, utility and clarity of the information to be collected, and the use of automated collection techniques or other forms of information technology to minimize the information collection burden.

articles.summary: Stay up to date on the latest in health tech, digital health and health AI news with this weekly brief.

articles.title: Chutes & Ladders—Alignment Healthcare shuffles leadership team; Highmark hires former Optum CEO
articles.summary: Welcome to this week's Chutes & Ladders, our roundup of hirings, firings and retirings throughout the industry. Please submit the good news—or the bad—from your shop, and we will feature it here at the end of each week.

articles.title: Epic, Oracle and Cleveland Clinic among companies to joining CMS prior authorization initiative
articles.summary: A slew of additional "early adopters" from different corners of the industry said they will tackle the workflow, technical and operational barriers that have stymied adoption of electronic prior authorization, CMS said this week.

articles.title: Bipartisan lawmakers reintroduce bill barring PBMs from owning pharmacies
articles.summary: A bipartisan group of lawmakers in both chambers of Congress has reintroduced a bill aimed at barring companies from owning both a pharmacy benefit manager and retail pharmacies.

articles.title: Fierce Healthcare Fundraising Tracker '26: 9amHealth picks up $26M; Anomaly nabs $17M for payer intelligence platform
articles.summary: Keep up with all the venture capital dollars being funneled into the health tech and digital health industries.

articles.title: Chromie Health picks up $2M in pre-seed funding, launches SMS AI-powered nurse staffing agent
articles.summary: Chromie Health CEO and co-founder Douglas Ford told Fierce Healthcare the tool has already helped fill more than 35,000 last-minute nursing shifts.

articles.title: Court approves sale of CVS' Omnicare unit to GenieRx Holdings
articles.summary: CVS' Omnicare unit has secured court approval to sell its business to virtual care company GenieRx Holdings, the healthcare giant announced Thursday.

articles.title: University of California, union reach late-night deal to avert system-wide strike
articles.summary: A union representing 25,000 UC Health service and patient care workers struck an 11th hour tentative agreement it says includes substantial pay increases and affordable healthcare rates.

articles.title: Viz.ai launches AI-powered pulmonary care platform
articles.summary: The new Viz Pulmonary Suite combines acute and chronic pulmonary workflows into a single solution, which the company says, is the first of its kind for such care.

articles.title: Nearly 80% of payers prefer vendor-built AI solutions, survey finds
articles.summary: Seventy-five percent of respondents report plans to spend an average of $10 million on AI over the course of the next three to five years.

articles.title: Salesforce Ventures, Echo Health Ventures back Optura's $17.5M series A to track AI performance
articles.summary: Optura claims that more than $2 billion in AI initiatives currently run on its platform, with $120 million in tracked value at a 700% return on AI investment on in-flight initiatives.

articles.title: CMS to withhold $1.3B in Medicaid funds from California, puts state officials on notice about fraud
articles.summary: Just hours after the Trump administration announced action against fraud in the hospice and home health spaces, Vice President JD Vance put state regulators on notice that the feds are poised for further action.

articles.title: Docs more burned out, skeptical of AI than nurses, survey report finds
articles.summary: Across many measures, doctors struggle more than nurses, the report found, and have a more negative view of how their organizations use AI.

articles.title: NYU Langone Health says it received grand jury subpoena over gender-affirming care
articles.summary: The health system disclosed that it is "one of several institutions" facing a criminal investigation over its delivery of the services to minors, an escalation in the Trump administration's pressure campaign.
